conclusions: Six first-step cases completed on two simulated USB controllers with the production signed kernel, actual fd release/last-fd/dup, original deadline, retained terminal bytes, cancelled request, ordered actual model cleanup and Revoking-to-Free. These are not physical host/libusb holds or RF.

Six idle STOP refusal cases retain original VM FAIL and exact EIO/status0b/opcode1002 RecoveryBlocked, Faulted/zero credits and Cancelled/Unknown. Independent capture corroboration proves the refused model reply; arbitrary failed startup cannot qualify.

The peer remained independent Setup with Diagnostic ownership and three matching captured MAC queries before/during/after. This is simulated query isolation, not active Ready survivor or four-device physical concurrency.
Only step0 is covered; later initialization steps, real firmware cleanup/quiesce, current real startup, active Ready peer, normal scheduler concurrency, RF regression and recovery are still required.
Model success and model refusal are separate. A permissive synthetic idle STOP does not establish real firmware support; failed cleanup is not normalized to Off/Ready/Free.

Root cause of physical WS73 startup/bulk timeout remains unknown; no new physical reset, host module/kernel/service installation or udev/PM change occurred. Previously authorized ganged hub cycles are not independent automatic recovery.
Historical real WS73 dual-device evidence and original S0-S6/issues scope are preserved; no partial success closes a whole issue.
